subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Alfred Peet: Godfather of American Specialty Coffee
description: A quick win: understand Alfred Peet: Godfather of American Specialty Coffee.

hook.text: Dutch immigrant Alfred Peet opened Peet's Coffee in Berkeley, California in 1966—and changed how Americans tasted coffee.

buildup.text: Peet grew up in his father's coffee trade in the Netherlands. He was appalled by the weak, stale coffee Americans drank.

discovery.text: Peet roasted small batches of high-quality beans dark and fresh. Customers tasted the difference immediately—it was a revelation.

twist.text: Three early customers—Baldwin, Siegl, and Bowker—founded Starbucks in 1971 using Peet's roasting methods.

climax.text: Without Peet, there's no Starbucks, no specialty movement, no third wave. He lit the match; America's coffee revolution followed.

punchline.text: One immigrant, one small shop, one higher standard. American coffee was reborn.

quiz.question: How did Alfred Peet influence Starbucks?
options: Three of his customers founded Starbucks using his methods and standards

details.summary: Dutch immigrant Alfred Peet opened Peet's Coffee in Berkeley, California in 1966, introducing Americans to dark-roasted, high-quality beans at a time when most drank weak, canned coffee. He directly trained the founders of Starbucks, making him the godfather of American specialty coffee.
details.whyItMatters: Without Alfred Peet, Starbucks and the entire American specialty coffee revolution might never have happened. His vision transformed how America thinks about coffee quality.
takeaways: Peet opened his Berkeley shop in 1966 with dark European-style roasts
He personally trained the original Starbucks founders
His influence launched the American specialty coffee movement

faq.question: How did Alfred Peet influence the founding of Starbucks?
faq.answer: The three original Starbucks founders were regular customers at Peet's. He taught them about sourcing and roasting, supplied their first beans, and inspired them to open their own shop in Seattle in 1971.

faq.question: What made Peet's approach to coffee different from what Americans were drinking?
faq.answer: Americans in the 1960s mostly drank weak coffee from canned pre-ground blends. Peet roasted small batches of high-quality beans dark and fresh, creating a richer, more flavorful experience that shocked and delighted customers.
